ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(kinematics): iterate inverse_kinematics to convergence (#3613)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(kinematics): iterate inverse_kinematics to convergence (#3613)

* fix(kinematics): iterate inverse_kinematics to convergence

placo's solver.solve(True) performs a single Newton step. From a
non-trivial seed, one step leaves significant residual position error
(~29 mm on a 100 mm target on the lerobot/unitree-g1-mujoco exo_left
URDF). The teleop loop is supposed to converge across frames, but with
initial_guess_current_joints=True the seed is reset every frame to the
lagging motor positions -- so it never converges in practice and the
EE drifts on a held target.

Loop the placo solve internally with a max_iters parameter (default 8,
enough for any in-workspace target). Calls update_kinematics() inside
the loop so each Newton step builds on the previous step's state.

Adds a regression test that downloads the exo_left URDF from the
existing lerobot/unitree-g1-mujoco HF repo (matching the pattern used
elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. unitree_g1/g1_kinematics.py).  Test
fails on lerobot 0.5.1 (~29 mm residual) and passes after this fix
(<1 mm).

* Delete tests/model/test_kinematics.py

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(datasets): answer delta queries through cached single-column view…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(datasets): answer delta queries through cached single-column views (#4314)

* fix(datasets): answer delta queries through cached single-column views

Since datasets 4.4, a custom transform disables the lazy-Column fast
path, so both hf_dataset[key][indices] and hf_dataset[indices][key]
fetch and decode entire rows. On image datasets this decodes every
embedded camera image of every queried row just to read a
low-dimensional column like action.

Route delta queries (and the video timestamp lookup) through cached
select_columns views instead: a zero-copy schema projection that
restores true column access. ~200x faster on the query, 46x per sample
end-to-end on an image dataset with a 50-step action chunk.

Fixes #2895

* fix(datasets): include the transform in the column-view cache key

set_transform() mutates hf_dataset in place, so dataset identity alone
cannot invalidate the cached single-column views: a view built under the
previous transform would keep answering delta queries with it. Compare
the transform recorded at view-build time and rebuild when it changes.

Addresses review feedback on #4314.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: Fix reset config joint positions encoding (#4545)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
Fix reset config joint positions encoding (#4545)

* fix(envs): type fixed_reset_joint_positions as list[float]

draccus cannot encode a dataclass field annotated `Any`: encoding calls
`isinstance(value, typing.get_origin(t) or t)`, and `typing.Any` is not
usable with `isinstance`. Any config that sets
`ResetConfig.fixed_reset_joint_positions` therefore raises:

    TypeError: typing.Any cannot be used with isinstance()

This fires in `lerobot.rl.learner` at the first statement after config
parsing -- `logging.info(pformat(cfg.to_dict()))` (learner.py:166) --
before the dataset, policy or gRPC server are constructed. Every HIL-SERL
config sets a reset pose, so the learner cannot start at all, in
simulation or on hardware. `lerobot_train.py:272` makes the same call.

The field is consumed only by `gym_manipulator.make_robot_env`, which
passes it to `RobotEnv(reset_pose=...)`, and every shipped example config
supplies a plain list of joint positions -- so `list[float] | None` is the
accurate annotation. `Any` remains imported and used elsewhere in the file.

Verified against the published example config
(lerobot/config_examples rl/gym_hil/train_config.json): the learner now
reaches "Starting learner thread" with the gRPC server up and the offline
replay buffer populated.

* docs(envs): update HIL-SERL reset positions type

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(datasets): native support for LeRobot datasets stored as LanceDB…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(datasets): native support for LeRobot datasets stored as LanceDB datasets (#4363)

Add Lance storage support for LeRobot datasets

* Add a reader-level storage abstraction with BaseDatasetReader, keeping
    LeRobotDataset as the single public dataset API. The existing
    DatasetReader remains the default lerobot backend, while
    LanceDatasetReader provides Lance-backed storage selected through
    storage_format in meta/info.json.
* Add batched Lance reads with support for delta timestamps, padding masks,
    episode subsets, language columns, depth features, and parity with the
    existing LeRobot reader semantics.
* Add efficient local and remote video decoding from Lance blob columns.
    Video byte indexes are used to issue coalesced, keyframe-aligned ranged
    reads for each batch, backed by sparse seekable sources and decoder caches.
    Video preparation and decoding are parallelized and work with RGB and
    depth video paths.
* Support local paths and remote dataset roots including s3://, gs://,
    file://, and hf://buckets/.... Dataset metadata is stored in a Lance
    meta table and materialized locally for compatibility with
    LeRobotDatasetMetadata, with revision, authentication, cache consistency,
    and path-safety handling.
* Add dataset integrity validation for frame counts, episode boundaries, and
    referenced video files, plus consistent float64 timestamp tolerance checks
    across video decoders.
* Integrate Lance readers with dataset factories, training/evaluation,
    multiprocessing DataLoaders, Groot, depth output units, and repository
    configuration while preserving the existing behavior for standard LeRobot
    datasets.
* Add optional lancedb and lancedb-convert dependencies and tests covering
    reader parity, remote-root factory routing, multiprocessing, language
    columns, metadata safety, video/depth decoding, and backend selection.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(datasets): keep small splits from dropping episodes in split_data…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(datasets): keep small splits from dropping episodes in split_dataset (#4001)

* fix(datasets): keep small splits from dropping episodes in split_dataset

Splitting by fractions rounded each split with int(total_episodes * fraction).
When a fraction rounded down to zero the split was skipped, which dropped both
the split and its episodes even when the fractions summed to 1.0. For example
{"train": 0.9, "val": 0.1} on 5 episodes returned only a 4-episode train split
and silently lost the fifth episode.

Allocate the leftover so every episode lands in exactly one split, and borrow a
single episode from the largest split to fill any positive-fraction split that
rounds to zero. Splits with more requested splits than episodes now raise
instead of dropping data.

* fix(datasets): reject negative split fractions and warn on zero ones

A negative fraction passed the sum <= 1.0 check and leaked a negative
count into the leftover arithmetic, so validate that every fraction is
non-negative next to that check.

An explicit zero fraction (e.g. {"train": 0.9, "val": 0.1, "test": 0.0})
is still skipped, but now logs a warning instead of dropping the split
silently, matching the rest of this function's no-quiet-loss behavior.

* refactor(datasets): trim split-fraction comments and tests per review

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(tests): fix peft cli test (#4477)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(tests): fix peft cli test (#4477)

`--peft.method` is a strict prefix of `--peft.method_type`, so argparse's
`allow_abbrev` expanded it silently. draccus 0.11 sets `allow_abbrev = False`,
so the flag stopped resolving when #4033 bumped the pin from 0.10.0 to 0.11.6
and all three tests now exit at argument parsing.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(rl): guard learner checkpoint saving against non-positive save_fr…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(rl): guard learner checkpoint saving against non-positive save_freq (#4479)

`save_freq` is documented as "a non-positive value disables periodic saving,
keeping only the final checkpoint", and the RL learner inherits the field from
TrainPipelineConfig. Its raw `optimization_step % save_freq` never honoured
that: 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, and -1 saves on every step because
`step % -1` is always 0.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(pi05): add optional training-time RTC (#4056)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(pi05): add optional training-time RTC (#4056)

feat(pi05): add optional training-time RTC

Adds opt-in training-time Real-Time Chunking to pi0.5 via
policy.rtc_training_max_delay (defaults to 0). When enabled, training samples a fully denoised
action prefix per example, accomplishing this by supplying per-action flow timesteps (1 for prefix, 0 for the rest), and
computing the flow loss only on the generated postfix. Trained
checkpoints run with --inference.rtc.mode=trained; guided
RTC remains the default for ordinary checkpoints.
